clue.text: Took off for hurried round tour

indicators.note: round means the word for hurried is placed all around the word for tour

parts.note: hurried means sped
a tour is a trip

explanation.surface: Someone set off around a whirlwind tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took off' reads as departed, but here it means removed, as clothes are.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip clothing is to remove it, so took off and stripped are past-tense synonyms.

clue.text: Holder of successive court actions

parts.note: a suit is a legal action in court
a case is also a legal action in court

explanation.surface: Someone holds the record for one lawsuit after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'successive' tells you the two court actions follow one another.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitcase is a container for carrying clothes, so it holds things.

clue.text: Resort to build on mountains

indicators.note: on means the first piece sits on top of the second in this down answer

parts.note: to rear a building is to put it up
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: A holiday resort is to be built up in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday spot; read it as re-sort, to sort again.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-sort things is to put them in a new order, which is to rearrange them.

clue.text: Insist on newspapers

explanation.surface: Demanding that the newspapers do something.
explanation.definitionFit: To press a point is to insist on it; the press is the newspapers collectively.

clue.text: Elaborate but simple once

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife, so once
plain means simple

explanation.surface: Something once simple has become elaborate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elaborate' reads as an adjective, ornate, but it is the verb, to give details.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate on something is to set out its details, which is to explain it.

clue.text: Prizes for servicemen

explanation.surface: Awards handed out to soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prizes' is the verb, as in prising open a lid, not awards.
explanation.definitionFit: To prize (prise) a box open is to force it; the armed forces are the military's servicemen.

clue.text: Start to speak without a single drink

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the speaking word goes around the rest

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally
I is the Roman numeral one, a single unit
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Begin to talk without having had a single drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: ORATE goes round I and GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to begin or bring into being, so it means to start.

clue.text: Mob leader found in stupor gets break in sentence

indicators.note: found in means the leading letter is placed inside the word for a stupor

parts.note: a coma is a deep stupor

indicators.note: leader means only the first letter of mob is taken

explanation.surface: A gang boss is discovered unconscious and gets a prison break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break in sentence' suggests time off a prison term; it is a pause in a written sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A comma marks a short pause in a written sentence.

clue.text: Reason for saint's torment unknown.

indicators.note: torment means the letters of saint are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
Y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Why a holy man should suffer is a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason in the sense of a sound mind is sanity.

clue.text: Raven, extremely pensive, once flew, it is said

parts.note: Grip is the talking raven in Dickens's novel Barnaby Rudge

indicators.note: extremely means only the extreme letters of pensive, first and last, are used

explanation.surface: A thoughtful raven took flight long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like flu: grippe is an old name for influenza, hence 'once'. Grip is the raven in Barnaby Rudge.
explanation.definitionFit: Grippe is the old French-derived word for influenza, which sounds like 'flew'.

clue.text: Robber dropping money is far from pleased

indicators.note: dropping means the word for money is let fall out of the robber's word

parts.note: a pirate is a robber at sea
P stands for pence, a sum of money

explanation.surface: A thief who loses the takings is unhappy about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means angry, which is about as far from pleased as one can get.

clue.text: Individual has very small distance to cover to obtain fruit

indicators.note: to cover means the word for an individual goes around the very small distance

parts.note: an individual is a person
one millimetre, a very small distance, is I (Roman one) followed by MM

explanation.surface: Someone has only a short way to go to pick some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The very small distance is 1 mm, with the 1 written as the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: The persimmon is an orange, tomato-like fruit from a tree grown in Asia and America.

clue.text: Unscrupulous' dealer has diamonds, perhaps, to go on display

annotationWithheld.why: Unscrupulous dealer has diamonds, perhaps, to go on display (4-5): CARDS (diamonds, perhaps) + HARP (go on) leaves 'display' with no job; no reading found that uses it
annotationWithheld.clue: Unscrupulous' dealer has diamonds, perhaps, to go on display

clue.text: It's not proper to sleep in it

indicators.note: in means the word for sleep is placed inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: A remark that sleeping in a particular place is improper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' at the start is only a link; the IT in the answer comes from 'it' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or inappropriate, so it describes something that is not proper.

clue.text: Paper leads with char's complaint

indicators.note: leads with means the word for paper comes first, followed by the next piece

parts.note: The Sun is a British newspaper
to char is to burn

explanation.surface: A newspaper runs a cleaning lady's grievance as its lead story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' suggests a British cleaning lady, but it is the verb to scorch; 'complaint' is an ailment, not a grievance. The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be a minor bodily ailment, and sunburn is one caused by too much sun.

clue.text: Unbalanced article on, staff at College opening

indicators.note: opening means this piece goes first, at the start of the answer
on means the article sits above the next piece in this down answer

parts.note: up means in residence at a university
the is the definite article
a pole is a staff

explanation.surface: A lopsided item about the staff at a college's opening ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: To be up is British for being in residence at university; 'opening' puts UP at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Up the pole is British slang for mad or mentally unbalanced.

clue.text: Permit giving directions to island retreat

parts.note: E and N are the compass directions east and north

indicators.note: retreat means the island's name goes backwards, as an army retreating goes back

parts.note: Elba is the island where Napoleon was exiled

explanation.surface: Permission is given with directions to an island hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks like a noun for a hideaway, but it turns ELBA round to give ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable someone is to allow them to do something, the same as to permit.

clue.text: Varsity sportsman, for example, hit bull to order

indicators.note: to order means the letters are arranged in a new sequence

explanation.surface: A university athlete, say, strikes the bullseye on command.
explanation.walkthrough: A Light Blue is a Cambridge University sportsman, after its colours; Oxford's are the Dark Blues.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge sportsmen who represent the university against Oxford are known by its light blue colour.

clue.text: Repeats parts of treatise

indicators.note: parts of means the word treatise is broken up and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Sections of a treatise say the same thing again.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to say or do again, so iterates is a synonym for repeats.

clue.text: Unwanted: creature about to return — could be badger

parts.note: a pest is an unwanted creature, such as vermin

indicators.note: to return means the short word for about is turned back

parts.note: re means about, as in business letters

explanation.surface: An unwanted animal that turns back might be a badger.
explanation.walkthrough: The badger seems to be the creature, but here it is the verb to nag; 'to return' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to harass them with repeated demands, which is to pester them.

clue.text: Remember to ring again

explanation.surface: A reminder to phone back.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall is to remember; to re-call someone is to phone them a second time.

clue.text: Cargo for French crew

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Goods shipped for a French boat crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is the goods carried by a ship, train or lorry, the same as cargo.

clue.text: Confounded stage journalist!

parts.note: a floor is a stage or level of a building
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: An exclamation of annoyance at a theatre critic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confounded' looks like a mild oath; here it means baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Floored means knocked flat by a problem, so baffled or confounded.

clue.text: Desperado seen in scrap and put inside

indicators.note: put inside means and is placed within the word for a scrap

parts.note: a bit is a scrap

explanation.surface: An outlaw spotted in a fight is arrested and jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' suggests a fight, but it means a small piece, BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a lawless robber, the kind of reckless outlaw called a desperado.

clue.text: A menial is humble

parts.note: base and menial both mean lowly

explanation.surface: A lowly servant is a humble person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humble' reads as an adjective but is the verb, to bring someone low.
explanation.definitionFit: To abase someone is to lower them in dignity, which is to humble them.

clue.text: Forsee taking a month going over old city

indicators.note: going over means the month sits above the city in this down answer

parts.note: Aug is short for August, a month
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Predicting a month spent travelling across an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Forsee' for foresee. 'taking' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To augur is to predict or portend what is coming.

clue.text: Contributions from rich set, or just one giving out notes?

indicators.note: contributions from means the letters of these words are pooled and remade into something new

explanation.surface: Donations come from a wealthy circle, or from a single person handing out banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving out notes' suggests handing out money, as the rich set might, but the notes are musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorister sings in a choir, one voice among many sending out musical notes.

clue.text: I am to get old picture

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: Someone is told they will grow old in a portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a likeness or representation, such as a picture.

clue.text: It may: encircle a champion boxer.

definitions.text: It may: encircle a champion boxer

parts.words: It may: encircle a champion boxer
parts.note: the boxer is the dog breed, and a prize-winning one wears a band around its neck

explanation.surface: A belt or ring around a title-holding fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: A champion boxer suggests a prizefighter's belt; the boxer is in fact a breed of dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog collar is the band fastened around a pet's neck, boxer breed included.

clue.text: Parcel 'incurs a charge when sent back

indicators.note: when sent back means the word for a charge is written in reverse

parts.note: a toll is a charge for using a road or bridge

explanation.surface: A package costs a fee when it is returned to sender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parcel' is the verb, as in parcel out; 'when sent back' turns TOLL into LLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To parcel something out is to divide and hand it round in shares, which is to allot it.

clue.text: Army runs, to secure objective

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
to get something is to secure it

explanation.surface: Soldiers make dashes to capture their goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A target is the goal or aim one works towards, the same as an objective.

clue.text: Unemployment list incomplete, needs revision

indicators.note: revision means the letters are revised into a new order
incomplete means the word list loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut short

explanation.surface: A jobless register that is unfinished needs to be revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts LIST to LIS, and 'revision' rearranges LIS with NEEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness is the state of having no work to do, a sense of unemployment.
